contents.notes: Title of work mentioned in explicit; treatise begins with apologies of the Trinity and Incarnation, then moves to a defense of the practice of spiritual fatherhood and confession; addressed to the Coptic patriarch Mark III (1166-1189) and the bishops of Upper Egypt; section on confession written in support of the Copt Marqus ibn Qunbar, who promoted private confession to a spiritual master instead of the more traditional method of confession over the raising of the censer; author sets out in his preface to defend these doctrines by citing scriptural and patristic testimonies; excerpts from various Church Fathers such as John Cassian, fol. 103r-107r, and Basil of Caesarea, fol. 113v-117v, 132v-144v; excerpts from the lives of the Egyptian Desert Fathers, fol. 121v-123v
